reason: Neuromuscular transmission failure, tubular-aggregate muscle pathology and a glycosylation disorder support the primary axes. Retinoschisis in 2/4 supports ocular involvement; medium confidence reflects limited sampling.
The definition establishes hepatic destruction by a liver fluke. Hepatic and infectious_immune apply; gastrointestinal involvement need not be inherited from the broader helminthiasis parent.

Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining cardiomyopathy and encephalopathy supports all three primary axes. Retinopathy in 1/1 supports ocular involvement with limited certainty; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
Gamma-sarcoglycanopathy is a skeletal muscular dystrophy. A neurological ancestor does not establish nerve damage, and the evidence does not establish common direct cardiac or pulmonary involvement.
Combined immunodeficiency warrants infectious_immune. The record establishes no additional cytopenia, marrow disease or other blood pathology requiring a separate haematologic label.

Interferonopathy and cerebral injury define the primary axes. Thrombocytopenia in 3/5 and respiratory insufficiency in 4/4, with documented ARDS, support involvement. Less severe cardiac findings are reasonably excluded by the cap.

Neurodevelopmental disability defines the syndrome. Structural skeletal abnormalities in 2/2, great-artery transposition in 1/2 and eyelid dysfunction from ptosis in 1/3 support the involved axes; small samples justify medium confidence.

The tumour originates in the paranasal sinuses, explicitly covered by pulmonary. Salivary or gastrointestinal origin cannot be inferred from the broader histological parent; metastatic risk adds no axis.

Pituitary deficiency and polydactyly define the primary axes. Developmental disability/seizures in 2/2 and cleft palate in 1/3 support neurologic and gastrointestinal involvement. The cap reasonably excludes the isolated urinary finding.
Sebaceous carcinoma is a skin-appendage malignancy, supporting dermatologic despite its vulvar location. The sebaceous carcinoma parent does not establish ocular origin for this subtype.
